Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you help me shape this into a prompt for a short handoff note for the next crew at Harbor Street Community Kitchen. it was the saturday lunch shift, 11am to 2pm, six volunteers were on shift and the plan was 36 packed lunches. by 1:30, 31 had been served and five were still on the table. the soup station was lentil soup, and the sandwich station packed cheese and cucumber sandwiches. there were two crates of carrots delivered before the shift, but they weren't part of the lunch packs. include the useful details without guessing why five lunches were left or what happened after 1:30. the handoff note should be calm and practical, not promotional, and should help the next crew see what was done and what they need to know. preserve these spoken notes exactly as quotes: “The lentil soup is ready at 11:15.” “Please keep the allergen cards beside the serving trays.” don't turn either quote into a paraphrase. mention that the allergen cards need to stay by the trays, but don't claim anything about a particular allergy or whether the cards were checked. don't make up a date, names for the volunteers, or extra kitchen procedures. keep it short enough to read during a shift, and use a simple title if that fits. make the prompt clear about the handoff note being based only on these details, not write the note itself.", "output": "Write a short, calm, practical handoff note for the next crew at Harbor Street Community Kitchen, based only on the details below. Use a simple title if appropriate. Do not invent a date, volunteer names, reasons, later events, or additional kitchen procedures.

Details:
- The Saturday lunch shift ran from 11am to 2pm, with six volunteers on shift.
- The plan was to pack 36 lunches. By 1:30, 31 had been served and five remained on the table. Do not guess why they remained or what happened after 1:30.
- The soup station served lentil soup; the sandwich station packed cheese and cucumber sandwiches.
- Two crates of carrots were delivered before the shift, but were not part of the lunch packs.
- Note that the allergen cards need to stay beside the serving trays. Do not identify any particular allergy or claim that the cards were checked.

Include these spoken notes exactly as quotes, without paraphrasing them:
“The lentil soup is ready at 11:15.”
“Please keep the allergen cards beside the serving trays.”"}]
